transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-07-19
Start: 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Lewis Carter (CTO - Verdant), Anika Bose (Sr ML Eng), Harold Kim (Platform)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand integration needs for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus areas: SDK support (Python/TS), LangChain & LlamaIndex integrations, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks and POC bench requirements. Customer wants low-latency inference for document summarization and agent flows; data residency + encryption are top concerns.

Topics:
- SDKs, sample code and streaming support
- LangChain / LlamaIndex connector patterns
- Gateway/proxy (single egress vs per-region) and token management
- Rate limiting / quotas and burst behavior
- Observability hooks: traces, per-request tokens, cost breakdowns
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, VPC, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and Carlos our solutions engineer is here. Can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Lewis: Yeah, I'm Lewis, CTO at Verdant. We run a small payments data platform, and we're looking to add summarization + agent workflows across our user dashboards.
[00:15] Anika: Hi all, Anika - ML eng, I'll be doing the integration work. Main concerns are latency and cost per request.
[00:20] Harold: Harold, platform. Networking and compliance questions for us.
[00:24] Maya: Awesome. Carlos, want to kick off on the integration options?
[00:27] Carlos: Sure. So high level, Redwood offers Hosted API for fastest time to value, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for full isolation. For integrations we have first-class SDKs in Python and TypeScript, REST and gRPC endpoints, and streaming responses. We also provide connectors and examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex.
[00:47] Anika: Quick question - is the LangChain connector maintained by Redwood or community? I saw a repo but wasn't sure.
[00:52] Carlos: We maintain an official Redwood adapter for LangChain and a LlamaIndex example. Sometimes docs call it LongChain or LamaIndex in autogenerated text, so sorry for the noise. The examples show how to set up streaming, handle tokenization, and integrate the Redwood SDK with chain of docs.
[01:05] Lewis: For us streaming is useful because we do progressive summaries in the UI. Latency target is 200-400ms tail for short prompts (<=256 tokens). Can Dedicated meet that?
[01:15] Carlos: For small prompt sizes, Dedicated with pinned GPU pools typically hits low-100s ms tail latency; Hosted can too depending on model choice and routing. We often recommend Dedicated if you need consistent p99s and have steady QPS, since Hosted has multi-tenant variability.
[01:30] Anika: And what about cost tradeoffs? We looked at your docs but a concrete example for 50 qps sustained would help.
[01:36] Maya: We'll send an ROI calc for Hosted vs Dedicated. Quick back of envelope, Dedicated amortizes if sustained QPS and long-running sessions; Hosted is easier to test.
[01:45] Harold: Network/security, we run in AWS us-east-1. Can Redwood do VPC peering or private link? Also we require KMS integration for key management and audit logs for model calls.
[01:56] Carlos: Yes, Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed VPC deployment. We also support KMS/HSM integrations for both Dedicated and Private tiers and an audit log stream (S3/Kinesis). Hosted offers encrypted at rest and per-tenant segregation but not customer-managed KMS by default - we can discuss enterprise options.
[02:14] Lewis: For data residency we need logs to remain in our account and not be accessible to third parties. How is that handled?
[02:22] Carlos: Dedicated and Private give you that control. Hosted can be configured with stricter retention and export of logs into your account for compliance, but if you need absolute isolation Private is the path.
[02:31] Anika: Integration specifics - we use LangChain in Python and LlamaIndex to build retrieval. Can we run Redwood as a gateway/proxy in front of our models, or do we call Redwood from our gateway? We're trying to avoid leaking API keys in client apps.
[02:44] Maya: Two common patterns: 1) Client -> Your API -> Redwood Hosted/Dedicated (your server holds keys), 2) Deploy Redwood Private in your VPC with a local gateway, so calls never leave network. If you're on Hosted, you should always proxy through your backend or use Redwood's JWTs and short-lived tokens.
[03:02] Harold: Do you support request attribution / per-route quotas? We need to throttle per-tenant.
[03:07] Carlos: Yes, Redwood supports per-api-key and per-route rate limits, quotas, and burst settings. We also expose token-level usage metrics in the console and via our billing API for custom enforcement.
[03:20] Lewis: Observability - we need tracing correlated with our distributed traces. Any OpenTelemetry support?
[03:25] Carlos: We emit trace headers and support OpenTelemetry export hooks; you can ingest traces into your APM or ours. The console shows per-request latency/tokens/cost breakdown and you can stream raw events to your SIEM.
[03:37] Anika: About SDKs - is there support for caching prefixes / KV cache? Our retriever uses a prefix cache to speed up repeated queries.
[03:44] Carlos: The runtime does prefix and KV caching automatically for sessions; we give APIs to manage caches and prewarming. For LlamaIndex flows we show how to persist embeddings and manage retrieval hygiene. There's also automatic batching to improve throughput.
[03:58] Lewis: We're also exploring quantized model variants to reduce cost. Does Redwood handle model variants and automatic fallback?
[04:05] Carlos: Yes - the smart routing layer can route between variants, fall back to higher-capacity models, and automatic fallback policies can be configured for quality vs cost. Quantized variants are supported and we publish performance profiles.
[04:15] Harold: Any limit on QPS per account? We expect spikes during report runs.
[04:20] Carlos: Quotas are configurable; Hosted has soft limits and fixed burst windows, Dedicated is a capacity commit with predictable throughput and can be configured for burst capacity. We'll capture your spike profile and size the pool for the POC.
[04:33] Anika: For the LangChain example - do you have a repo that shows LLamaIndex + Redwood + Retriever + streaming to the UI?
[04:40] Carlos: Yes, I have a sample repo. I'll post it - it includes a gateway example, LongChain connector, and a tiny demo using Redux in the UI for streaming tokens. Note: auto-transcription sometimes shows "Redwood Dedicatedy" in titles, ignore that.
[04:55] Maya: On security docs - we'll send SOC2, penetration test summary, our encryption at rest and in transit details, and our audit log format.
[05:03] Lewis: Great. For the POC we want you to run a benchmark against our sample prompt set; we care about p50/p95/p99 and token cost. Can you do that in a Dedicated pilot?
[05:12] Carlos: Yes, we can provision a short Dedicated pilot for benchmarking. We'll need your sample prompts, expected concurrency and a day/time window. If you prefer Private we can discuss a short-term VPC deployment for the run.
[05:23] Harold: Licensing / procurement question - how does billing for Dedicated look? Is it monthly commit plus overages?
[05:29] Maya: Typical contract is a monthly reserved capacity with committed usage, with options for overage at a discounted tier. We'll include a sample SOW.
[05:37] Anika: One minor thing - we use LlamaIndex pinned to a custom retriever; will we need to rewrite a lot of code?
[05:44] Carlos: Minimal. LlamaIndex adapters are small; we provide example wrappers. The biggest lift is tokenization behavior differences and streaming handlers - we can pair-program the first integration.
[05:56] Lewis: Sounds good. Any showstoppers you foresee?
[05:59] Carlos: Nothing from our side; main gap is we need your exact QPS and retention/ingest patterns to size Dedicated correctly. Also, if you require HSM-backed keys in Hosted, that's an enterprise feature to scope.
[06:12] Maya: Recap and next steps - we'll send the security pack and pricing, Carlos will post the LangChain / LlamaIndex samples and gateway proxy example, Verdant will share sample prompts and VPC info, and we'll schedule a 30m POC bench next week.
[06:28] Lewis: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the materials.
[06:31] Maya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
